Q013-02.why: Both give a one-step-solve linear inequality in x and ask which listed value of x is (or, here, is NOT) a solution; same solve-then-check-choices reasoning, only the polarity of the ask flips.
Also 'which value of x satisfies 2x − 5 > ...', but x appears on both sides and the coefficient flip/negative division is the point of that item.

Q013-03.why: Unknown coordinate of a point on a line, but there the slope is given; here slope must be found from two points first.

Q013-05.why: Both use 2^(x+k) = 2^k·2^x; ACT item goes forward (g(x+3) = 8g(x)), this one goes in reverse to find the shift k.

Q013-06.why: Same Bayes/reverse-conditional template: base-rate percent for a group, percent with a trait in that group and in its complement, then P(group | trait). Only the context (screening test vs club/sport) and numbers change.
Same reverse-conditional ask from two groups, but subgroup counts are given directly rather than as percents of a percent base.

Q013-08.why: Both drop the altitude in an isosceles triangle with given equal sides and base, but ACT asks for area while this asks for sin of a base angle.

Q013-09.why: Right triangle with algebraic legs and Pythagorean/area link, but the given and asked quantities are reversed (area->hypotenuse vs hypotenuse->area) and setup differs (3x,4x vs x, x+7 quadratic).
